label: input token f/j/p/n during the original phase
explanation: Fires mostly in the original (input) phase (84% of mass) when the current input is f (36% of mass, active on 35% of f steps), j or p (about 12% each, ~24% rate) or n (10%, 15% rate). Weaker contributions come from z, g, e, r and the <DEL> step (11% of mass, 7.5% rate). Firing is more likely at early positions (t <= 3) and on the first occurrence of a token. The largest activations come in sequences whose first token is d or v, usually on f (or j/n/p) just before <DEL>, and on the <DEL> that follows. It is nearly silent in the copy phase (5% of mass) and rarely fires on digits, o or b. The token identity is not enough on its own: most f/j/p/n steps do not activate, and the context that decides this was not captured (dev F1 about 0.52).
